With a pneumatic yarn splicer clipped to her belt, she pinches two yarns together and pops the trigger to join them, then nudges the take-up roll by hand to check pick spacing and tension. 51-6091.00.careerTitle: Extruding & Forming Machine Setters, Operators, & Tenders, Synthetic & Glass Fibers
51-6091.00.sceneDescription: In a polymer fiber‑spinning bay, a Latina woman in her 30s leans into the line, using a stainless threading hook to draw a fresh bundle of molten‑cooled polyester filaments from the spinneret, through the quench cabinet and a ceramic eyelet, and around a humming godet roller toward the take‑up winder. With her gloved thumb she dials the godet nip‑pressure knob while watching the control panel’s tension readout to stabilize the yarn after a break. The heated spin pack, finish applicator bath, staggered godet rolls, and rotating bobbin frame crowd the foreground; far down the aisle, a smaller coworker checks a quench fan shroud. She wears safety glasses, sleeve guards, and cut‑resistant gloves, a small torque wrench and lint‑free swabs clipped at her belt beside a solvent bottle for cleaning a clogged spinneret pack.
